clue.text: Restless, little devil — one that is into explosive chemical

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
a, as in one of something

indicators.note: is into means the preceding piece goes inside what follows

parts.note: TNT, trinitrotoluene, is the classic explosive chemical
i.e. (id est) means 'that is'; here 'that' plus the 'is' of 'is into' gives the abbreviation IE

explanation.surface: A fidgety imp, apparently a creature that has got itself inside some explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is the Latin id est, abbreviated i.e.; TNT is trinitrotoluene.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless cannot keep still and wants things to happen now, which is being eager and fidgety.

clue.text: Rambling, wanting company — that's natural

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the company letters are taken out

parts.note: rambling talk is incoherent, disjointed

explanation.surface: A wandering, solitary walk is described as the most natural thing in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a synonym: INCOHERENT, from which CO is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inherent is built in, part of a thing's essential nature, hence natural to it.

clue.text: Old man left China

definitions.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate = mate), i.e. a friend

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, pa

explanation.surface: A dad has quit China, or so the line reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang 'china' means a mate, a close friend, which is exactly what a pal is.

clue.text: Harry — been to fight with prince — news ignored sign of a much bigger problem

definitions.text: sign of a much bigger problem

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so these letters are knocked into a new order
ignored says those letters are left out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
read as N's, the plural of N (new): two Ns

explanation.surface: Prince Harry's spat with his family, ignored by the press, hints at a much deeper rift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince; it is the anagram signal. BEEN TO FIGHT plus PRINCE has two extra Ns, and 'news' read as N's is exactly those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The tip of the iceberg is the small visible portion of a far larger hidden problem, an idiom from icebergs mostly being underwater.

clue.text: Get down on this festival dance floor at last

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the words dance and floor

parts.note: its final letter
its final letter

explanation.surface: An invitation to bust some moves on the dance floor at the end of a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' sounds like dancing, but the definition means obtain down feathers: eiderdown comes from this duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a sea duck whose soft breast feathers, eiderdown, are gathered for quilts and pillows.

clue.text: Hammer thrower dropping round with book for pound

indicators.note: in a down answer, dropping means the round letter sinks lower down the word

parts.note: Thor, the Norse god, throws his hammer Mjolnir
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An athletics report: the hammer thrower falls short in a round, then a book about pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer thrower' is not an athlete but the god THOR; the O drops one place to give THRO, then B is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound and to throb both describe a heavy, rhythmic beating, as of a heart or a headache.

clue.text: Dark web ultimately involved in transaction

indicators.note: involved in means this letter is wrapped up inside the next word's letters

parts.note: a sale is a transaction

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of web

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: Something shady about the dark web turning up in a dodgy deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark web' reads as one phrase, but 'Dark' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic word for black, so it serves as an adjective meaning dark.

clue.text: Direct familiar child's play

parts.note: straight means direct, without detour
forward means overfamiliar, presumptuous

explanation.surface: Instructions to direct a well-known children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' looks like the definition, which would also fit, but here it supplies only the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Child's play is something very easy, and a straightforward task is simple and uncomplicated.

clue.text: Reversible vest

indicators.note: reversible says the answer reads the same whichever way it is read

parts.note: the garment itself, whose name reads the same both ways

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversible' describes the word, not the garment: the three letters read the same backwards, and the thing is a vest-like panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bib is the numbered vest-like panel a runner or player wears over the shirt, and its name is palindromic.

clue.text: Judge in Provence is to atone for missing wine

parts.note: est is French for 'is', the language of Provence

indicators.note: missing means the wine is taken out of that word

parts.note: to redeem is to make amends for, atone for
red is wine

explanation.surface: A judge in the south of France must make amends after doing without wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb here: to esteem is to regard or consider.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something can mean to consider or reckon it so, as in 'I esteem it an honour', which is to judge it.

clue.text: It looks like a giant h-held beer in?

definitions.text: It looks like a giant h

indicators.note: in means the beer goes inside the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
IPA is India Pale Ale, a beer

explanation.surface: A stammering drinker swears his pint looks like a giant letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'h-held' splits the clue: 'h' ends the definition and 'held' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter landing pad is usually marked with a large letter H inside a circle.

clue.text: Dish dirt conclusively on teacher providing religious education for a bishop

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
for means the bishop's letter is replaced by religious education

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
RE is the school subject Religious Education

indicators.note: conclusively points to the last letter of dirt

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A gossip columnist offers dirt on a teacher who teaches religion in a bishop's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish dirt' reads as gossiping, but 'Dish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a dish of melted cheese on toast.

clue.text: Force field analysis research starts, having been put back

indicators.note: put back means the letters are read in reverse order
starts takes the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: its first letter
its first letter
its first letter

explanation.surface: A physics paper: force field analysis research gets postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force field' reads as one physics term, but 'Force' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The RAF, Royal Air Force, is Britain's air force, one of its armed forces.

clue.text: Buffoon Farage not mature about Brussels' rules primarily

indicators.note: not means those letters are left out of the name

parts.note: taken as written, the name of the Brexit politician
to age is to mature
C is circa, Latin for about
Brussels is the seat of the EU, the European Union

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of rules

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A political jibe: Nigel Farage, an immature clown, rails against EU regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage is the British Brexit campaigner; his surname is used as letters. C stands for circa, Latin for about.
explanation.definitionFit: A farceur is a joker or performer of farce, so a clown or buffoon.

clue.text: A brief dirge composed for Trumpton's brass band

indicators.note: a piece of music composed is put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A short funeral tune written for a small town's brass band.
explanation.walkthrough: Trumpton was a 1960s British children's TV show whose fire brigade (Pugh, Pugh, Barney McGrew...) played a band concert at the end of each episode.
explanation.definitionFit: In the TV series the town's firemen doubled as its brass band, playing in the bandstand.

clue.text: Virgin, say, feeling on edge

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means sitting above

parts.note: an air is a feeling or impression, as in an air of mystery
a line is an edge or boundary

explanation.surface: A nervous virgin, feeling on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' is Virgin Atlantic, the company, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin Atlantic is an example of a carrier that flies passengers, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Shock horror — Kent is extremely happy county

indicators.note: to shock is to jolt or upset, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: extremely takes the outer letters of happy

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Tabloid outrage: Kent is crowned the happiest county in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kent' is a county itself, a decoy; it is anagram fodder. The other county is in Yorkshire, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: North Yorkshire is a large county in northern England, England's biggest by area.

clue.text: Published books about United

indicators.note: about means the books go around the next letter; that the word about also contains the answer is a coincidence

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books
U is a standard abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A publisher's note on books written about a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: When a book is out, it has been released to the public, so it is published.

clue.text: Legend in dock according to hearsay

indicators.note: hearsay is what is heard, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a quay is a dock or wharf

explanation.surface: A famous figure is in court, at least according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legend' suggests a famous person or myth; here it is the explanatory table on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend of a map or chart is the key that explains its symbols.

clue.text: Iron Maiden covering right tracks — band provides content for channel — one might work there?

indicators.note: covering means the first pair goes around what follows

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of tracks

indicators.note: content means the inside of band, without its outer letters

parts.note: its middle letters

explanation.surface: Iron Maiden, the heavy metal band, putting out tracks for a TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Maiden' and 'band' suggest the heavy metal group, but 'Maiden' is the cricket term for an over with no runs, and the channel is the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferryman carries passengers across water, so he might work crossing the English Channel.

clue.text: Occupation on list unions organised here?

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: a registry is an official register or list
an office is a position or occupation

explanation.surface: A list of jobs, perhaps posted for trade unions to organise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unions' suggests trade unions; they are marriages, performed at the register office.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil marriages in Britain take place at a registry office, so wedding unions are arranged there.

clue.text: Fielders upset over splitting prize money?

indicators.note: splitting means the letter goes inside, breaking it apart
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, i.e. the letters reversed

parts.note: slips are fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper in cricket
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Cricket fielders are upset over sharing out the prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIPS upset gives SPILS, which the O then splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoils are the booty or gains taken in a contest, so something like prize money, hence the question mark.

clue.text: According to vacuous prince, heartless informer is the one who did wrong

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per the rules'

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of prince remain

parts.note: its first and last letters

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of that word

parts.note: a traitor betrays others, as an informer does

explanation.surface: An empty-headed prince claims the culprit is a heartless informer.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAITOR's central letter is I, so heartless gives TRATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A perpetrator is the person who commits a crime or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Schedules hill climbing on a sierra

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above
in a down clue, climbing means the word goes upward, reversed

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Timetables for climbing a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotas are rosters that schedule who does which duty and when.

clue.text: Some militia ransacks jewellery

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A militia raids a place and loots the jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental crown or headband, a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Appreciation of sea air, occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter, here the even ones

parts.note: its alternate letters

explanation.surface: An occasional liking for a breath of sea air.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an ear for music means having a feel or appreciation for it.

clue.text: Study Pakistan's opener during cricket for example

indicators.note: during means that letter comes in the middle of the next word

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect

indicators.note: opener takes the first letter of Pakistan's

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Analysing Pakistan's opening batsman during a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' is the sport in the surface, but here the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, which is to study.

clue.text: Knight finally takes one rook

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of takes

parts.note: its last letter
I is the Roman numeral one
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess move: the knight ends up capturing a rook.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is addressed by the title Sir, so the honorific stands for the man himself.

clue.text: Trump's slogan inspiring Liberal graduate to join revolutionary Union

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the whole lot is read backwards
to join means the next piece is attached after
inspiring means breathing in, so the slogan takes in the letter

parts.note: MAGA is Make America Great Again
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Trump's catchphrase inspires a liberal graduate to join a radical trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' covers everything before it, so the whole build is read backwards at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend or combination of things, so a union of parts.

clue.text: Maybe grease two zips

parts.note: to zip is to go fast, so zips gives GO
two says zip is taken a second time, now as nothing, zero: the letter O

explanation.surface: Perhaps grease will help a couple of stuck zips.
explanation.walkthrough: Zip as energetic movement gives GO, and zip as nil gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is any sticky or slimy substance, and grease is one example, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Stop striking to tackle branch

indicators.note: striking means striking out, so those letters are struck from the word

parts.note: rig is gear or tackle, as on a ship or for fishing

explanation.surface: A union call to end the strike and tackle the branch's grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop striking' reads as ending industrial action; instead TO is struck out of STOP, leaving SP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig, a little branch of a plant.

clue.text: Laurel & Hardy's fourth feature put on to entertain wife — relax

parts.note: Stan Laurel, of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy

indicators.note: the fourth feature, i.e. the fourth letter, of Hardy

parts.note: its fourth letter

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the wife's letter is taken inside

parts.note: to don is to put on clothes

explanation.surface: Laurel and Hardy's fourth film is screened to amuse a wife who needs to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' suggests a feature film, but here it means a letter of Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to come off duty, to stop being on alert, hence to relax.
